title: Predicting Pre-Owned Vehicle Prices with Lasso Regression
summary:
Developed and evaluated a regularized regression model using 21,647 pre-owned vehicle records. The analysis combined sparse feature engineering, 10-fold cross-validation, independent test-set evaluation, and automated feature selection to create a disciplined benchmark for data-driven vehicle pricing.

The selected model produced a validation RMSE of $8,084.68 and a test RMSE of $7,780.07 across 10,824 previously unseen vehicles. Lasso reduced model complexity by eliminating 3,033 of 4,808 modeled predictor terms while retaining signals from vehicle age, manufacturer, model, condition, mileage, drivetrain, location, and other characteristics.
focus: Regularized predictive modeling and out-of-sample validation
domain: Automotive retail and vehicle pricing analytics
scale: 21,647 vehicle records · 11 original predictors · 4,808 modeled terms · 10,824-record independent test set · 10-fold cross-validation
highlights: Prepared a mixed-variable dataset and verified that the supplied records contained no missing values
Converted high-cardinality categorical variables into a computationally efficient sparse model matrix
Created reproducible training and independent test samples using a fixed random seed
Selected the lasso penalty through 10-fold cross-validation without using the final test data
Evaluated predictive performance on 10,824 unseen vehicle records
Identified limitations involving pricing heterogeneity, high-cardinality predictors, and reliance on a single train-test split
statusNote: Academic analytics scenario developed for graduate coursework using a provided vehicle dataset. Results demonstrate the modeling process and should be interpreted as an analytical benchmark, not as a deployed pricing system or an automatic final-price recommendation.
